cover letter

The University of California, Office of the President, is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience. The full salary range shows the growth potential for this position and the pay scale is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Minimum 8 years relevant experience and/or equivalent combination of education and experience

Reporting to the Associate Director of Labor Operations, the Contract Implementation Manager applies labor relations, payroll, compensation, and systems expertise to support the implementation of wage, compensation, and benefits provisions contained in systemwide collective bargaining agreements. This role coordinates with labor relations professionals, compensation and payroll teams, UCPath, Benefits, Retirement, UC Legal, and other systemwide and location-based stakeholders to promote accurate, timely, and consistent implementation of contractual requirements. The Contract Implementation Manager develops implementation strategies, provides recommendations, monitors represented employee data and reporting requirements, and helps resolve complex issues involving labor relations systems, data, and processes. The role serves as a resource to labor relations, compensation, payroll, and other operational professionals; supports systemwide meetings related to contract implementation; supports data collection and reporting related to contract administration and union Requests for Information as needed; and identifies opportunities to improve processes affecting the represented employee population. The manager is expected to work independently with limited direction, exercise sound judgment, and address significant issues requiring labor relations expertise, political sensitivity, and coordination across multiple stakeholders. The role requires strong oral and written communication skills, knowledge of labor relations terminology and contractual requirements, and the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse internal and external contacts. The manager may lead process improvement initiatives and provide guidance to professional staff while operating within the direction and priorities established by the Associate Director of Labor Operations.

40% Contract Implementation and Systems Coordination: Coordinate the implementation of wage, compensation, benefits, and other applicable provisions of systemwide collective bargaining agreements in collaboration with Labor Relations Managers, Chief Negotiators, compensation and payroll professionals, UCPath, Benefits, Retirement, and other relevant stakeholders. Apply knowledge of contract language, payroll processes, data systems, and represented employee populations to support accurate and timely implementation across UC locations. Maintain implementation plans, logs, decision logs, and institutional records. Track implementation activities, identify outstanding issues, and coordinate follow-up to ensure contractual requirements and established timelines are met. Support systemwide meetings related to contract implementation and promote consistent practices across locations and bargaining units.

20% Contract Implementation Analysis and Recommendations: Analyze collective bargaining agreement language, implementation requirements, payroll and compensation processes, and represented employee data to identify potential issues and develop recommendations. Consult with labor relations colleagues, subject matter experts, UC Legal, Systemwide Compensation, UCPath, Payroll, Benefits, Retirement, and location representatives as needed to understand operational impacts and develop effective approaches. Provide subject-matter expertise during bargaining, settlement discussions, side-letter negotiations, and other labor relations processes to assess implementation feasibility, identify operational and systems impacts, inform proposals, and help develop language that can be implemented accurately and consistently. Identify implementation issues that may require additional review, escalation, or a systemwide response. Apply independent judgment and labor relations knowledge to address complex or sensitive matters while advancing the University’s contractual and operational objectives.

20% Data Management and Reporting: Coordinate and undertake the collection, review, organization, and reporting of represented employee data related to collective bargaining agreements, contract implementation and the represented employee population. Provide operational coordination and support for data collection efforts in response to formal Requests for Information from unions as needed. Work with appropriate UCOP offices and locations to clarify data needs, confirm data accuracy, maintain appropriate records, and support timely responses, including pulling, manipulating, and delivering large data sets based on stated (and sometimes unstated) needs, in addition to coordination and oversight. Identify data management or reporting concerns and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to resolve them.

10% Process Improvement and Systems Management: Identify and support the development and implementation of process improvements, protocols, and tools related to contract implementation, contract administration, payroll and compensation transactions, labor relations systems, data management, and reporting. Monitor implementation workflows and related records to promote completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness. Strategically leverage available systems and tracking tools, maintain effective document management practices, and recommend improvements that increase efficiency and reduce implementation errors across the UC system.

10% Coordination, Communication, and Operational Support: Serve as a resource to labor relations, compensation, payroll, and other professionals at UC locations and within the Office of the President. Coordinate actions among multiple offices, locations, and individuals to support contract implementation and resolve issues. Communicate implementation requirements, timelines, decisions, and outstanding issues clearly to relevant stakeholders. Identify matters requiring specialized review or additional direction and escalate them to the Associate Director of Labor Operations and other appropriate leaders. May provide guidance to professional staff and support supervision, coordination, or training activities as assigned.
10% Periodic travel to UCOP headquarters in Oakland, systemwide meetings and occasional attendance at bargaining as needed for strategic support of contract development.

Benefits: For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University visit: Benefits of Belonging
Working knowledge of HRIS and related systems and applications used to manage human resources, payroll, compensation, benefits, or financial data.
Knowledge of labor relations principles, practices, terminology, and processes, preferably in a higher education or similarly complex organizational environment.
Familiarity with collective bargaining agreements and the ability to interpret and apply contract provisions related to wages, compensation, benefits, payroll, data, and reporting.
Advanced data analysis and manipulation skills in Excel, Power BI, or similar data-management tools.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex contract, systems, data, and implementation issues clearly to diverse audiences.
Skill in coordinating projects, implementation activities, timelines, meetings, and follow-up actions involving multiple offices, locations, and stakeholders.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate complex or sensitive issues, identify potential impacts, and develop practical recommendations.
Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when addressing contract implementation and administration matters.

Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with labor relations professionals, Chief Negotiators, UCOP departments, UC locations, union representatives, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and complete work accurately within demanding and time-sensitive contractual, operational, and implementation deadlines.
Ability to identify process improvement opportunities and support the development and implementation of effective systems and contract administration practices.
Ability to maintain accurate records and protect confidential, sensitive, and legally protected information.
Ability to work independently with limited direction while appropriately seeking guidance, escalating issues, and keeping leadership and stakeholders informed.
Ability to provide guidance, training, and operational support to professional staff and other individuals involved in contract implementation and related systems or data processes.
